director.chapterArc: A long-form confession where Rook dismantles the group's worldview to reveal that all power sources are identical (The Path), culminating in the revelation of his past with Vera Kess and Homura, ending on a quiet note of shared burden.
director.restraintNote: Maintain an analytical distance. The narrator is observing a man unburdening himself; do not dramatize Rook's pain or make it melodramatic. Let the facts carry the weight. Pace should be steady and measured, accelerating slightly during descriptions of violence but returning to slow, deliberate clarity for definitions.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is grounded and explanatory. He speaks with the weight of a mentor who has waited years to say this. The tone is intimate but not soft; it carries the gravity of his history.
cues.from: "I was born at a place called Lowry Bend," said Rook, "which is about four hundred miles south and east of here, in country you've never heard of and wouldn't like, and there were a hundred and forty of us in it, and my mother did nothing with her hands.
cues.through: He said it without any particular weight.
cues.reason: Establishes Rook as the focalizer for this long confession.

cues.delivery: Narrative observation of Toren's realization. The word 'Homura' is a proper noun that lands with finality; do not emphasize it as magic, but as a specific place name.
cues.from: He let the word out into the firelight, and it sat there, and Toren thought: there it is. That's the first one. That's a name that's never been said in front of us.
cues.through: "Homura was one valley where it wasn't happening."
cues.reason: Shift from Rook's speech to Toren's internal processing.

cues.delivery: Brief reaction. Milo and Rook exchange a simple acknowledgment of the conflict that defined their early years.
cues.from: "And the second week I was there, a girl about a foot shorter than me stood in a corridor and told me that what my mother did with her hands was a party trick for people too backward to have been given a proper stone."

cues.delivery: The turning point of the story. Rook's voice becomes flatter as he describes his loss of belief in tradition. The description of Vera's injury must be clinical and physical.
cues.from: "She got hurt," said Rook. "Which is not the answer you're expecting, and it's the true one.
cues.through: "And somewhere in about the sixth hour of it — and I have had eleven years to be honest with myself about this, so I'll be honest with you — I stopped caring about the entire argument. Not decided against it. Stopped being able to locate it. I sat on a floor, and I wanted one thing, and the thing I wanted was for somebody to put their hands on that girl, and there was no part of me anywhere that cared what tradition the hands came out of or what the person holding them believed about where it came from.
cues.reason: Shift to the core mechanism of Rook's change.

cues.delivery: Definitions delivered with precision. 'The Path' and 'Satori' are technical terms in this context; treat them as such rather than mystical concepts.
cues.through: "I do the wall and the stone and the running thing," said Rook, "and there's a fourth, and I haven't got it, and there's people who'd tell you there's further to go after that, and I don't know, and I've stopped needing to."
cues.reason: Expository section requiring clarity over emotion.

cues.delivery: The description of the attack. Rook's voice is detached here; he describes a tactical failure and a theft with cold precision.
cues.from: "Cinder Company came over the wire on the eleventh of the ninth month, at about two in the morning, and burned the whole of it, and everyone in it."
cues.through: "Somebody paid them to do it. Somebody with something to lose if four hundred settlements stopped sorting people by which door they fell through." He put another stick on. "I don't know who, and I've asked in about sixty places, and I've got nothing, and that's the honest state of it."
cues.reason: Narrative shift to describing the violence.

cues.delivery: The realization of identity. Rook's voice is heavy with the weight of a secret finally spoken.
cues.from: Toren felt the whole thing arrive about a second before it landed.
cues.through: "Eleven years since the valley. Nine since the lane. And for the first six of them, I was a man carrying two entirely separate holes, and then a bootmaker put a chit on a table and turned it over, and they were one hole, and they had been one hole the whole time, and I had been living next to it for six years like a man sleeping in a house with a body in it."

cues.delivery: Rook's direct address to Dessa. He is explaining a profound truth about her capability; the tone is serious and validating.
cues.from: "Fifteen days ago," he said, "on a night when nobody was watching you, you sat down on the ground with a stone in your hands, and you did not want anything, and the door went, and you filled straight off the whole of it for four seconds, and it felt like half a night to you because you were not filling through a door, and there is no clock on the other side of one.
cues.through: "Which is why I wouldn't talk to you about it," said Rook. "Not because it was small. Because I could not open my mouth about your four seconds without the whole of tonight coming out of it, and I wasn't ready, and I made you carry that for fifteen days on your own, and it's the worst thing I've done since I've known any of you."

cues.delivery: The physical reveal of Vera's stone. Rook handles it with reverence; the narration should reflect this tactile detail.
cues.from: He took it out of his coat pocket.
cues.through: "It was cut for a fifteen-year-old girl with small hands," said Rook. "I've had to hold it wrong for eleven years."
cues.reason: Focus on the object as a symbol.

cues.delivery: Wyck's question is direct and challenging. Rook's refusal to give his name is a boundary; the tone should be firm but not hostile.
cues.reason: Shift in dynamic as Wyck asserts himself.

cues.delivery: Rook's final answer to Toren. He is protective of the boy's understanding; the tone is gentle but firm.
cues.from: "It's called a Satori," he said. "The same word. Her people gave the thing and the state the same name on purpose, and I've never met anybody else who could tell me why.
cues.through: "Ask me again when you can hear me say it and still weigh it. That'll be in about a year, and I'll tell you when I think you've got there, and until then keep it under your shirt."
cues.reason: Closing exchange between mentor and student.

cues.delivery: The resolution. The group settles into silence; Rook falls asleep. The narration should be quiet and observational.
cues.from: Nobody went to bed for a long time, and nobody said much, and Toren could not afterward reconstruct any of the last hour of it in order: Milo asking what the cook at Homura had been like, and Rook answering, at length, and almost smiling; Senna asking whether Orrin Vell had been a tall woman and being told no, she was five foot nothing and everybody was terrified of her; Dessa sitting for twenty minutes with her hands open on her knees and her eyes shut in front of all of them for the first time ever, and getting nothing, and not minding.
cues.through: Then he did a thing Toren had never once seen him do, and did it without any ceremony at all: he lay down on his side by the fire with his coat pulled over his shoulder and the small grey stone shut up in his fist, and he was asleep inside a minute, and he slept until it was light.
cues.reason: Return to base narrator stance for the scene's end.

pauses.reason: Speaker reset and narrative beat: Toren's realization that they are at a turning point.
Emphasis on the antagonist group name; isolates this threat as a specific entity.

pauses.reason: Micro-pause for sensory detail (fire tick) before the violence description begins.

Isolating the third person mentioned in Rook's count; adds weight to this nameless victim.

pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Dessa reacts physically to the revelation about her power.

pauses.after: "It came off the floor of the long room at about ten past two in the morning on the eleventh of the ninth month," he said, "and it is the only thing I own, and it has been in my hand every day for eleven years, and nobody has asked me one question about it in all that time because a man with an Ember is the least remarkable thing in the world."
pauses.reason: Pause for Toren's realization of what 'Oh' means; allows connection between stone and Vera.

pauses.after: "That's what you've been standing in a line for," said Rook. "That's the whole of it. I'm teaching you the Path, which is the only thing I've got that's worth anything, and I started doing it on purpose the morning after that fire, and I have not told you because I could not say one word of it without saying all of tonight."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Rook explains the purpose of their journey; pause before Wyck's question.
Emphasis on Wyck's observation of Rook's callsign; isolates the metaphor for his identity.
